response.sql:
WITH g AS (
 SELECT ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id,
 p.product_color AS product_color,
 AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity,
 AVG((ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio
 FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
 JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id
 JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
 GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, p.product_color
), r AS (
 SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_ratio,
 RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_color ORDER BY avg_quantity IS NULL, avg_quantity DESC) AS rnk
 FROM g
)
SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_ratio, rnk
FROM r
WHERE rnk <= 3

assumptions.assumption: The product is found via the matched order item's product_id (Order_Items -> Products), since the request says to match to the order item and then bring in the product's color. Line items with a NULL order_item_id drop out of the inner join (the column is NOT NULL anyway).
product_quantity is stored as VARCHAR, so it is cast to a number before averaging.
Rows where derived_total_cost is zero or NULL yield a NULL ratio, which AVG ignores. In SQLite, division by zero returns NULL.
Products with a NULL color form their own group and partition, since they are not 'not found' rows.
